title: Achievements
summary: Every achievement, how to get it and what it pays. Secret ones stay secret.
text: Achievements follow you to every server. Each one pays out once, in the server where you unlock it, from the Reserve. Secret achievements are listed so you know they exist, but not how to get them. Rarities Every achievement FROM THE BOT

title: Who's who
summary: The characters of the Rend-Conomy: Marquez the shopkeeper, Chuck Alfrey at the docks, TODD the house, and Mr. Glaz.
text: The Rend-Conomy has a narrator, and it has a cast. These are the ones you'll meet. Marquez Marquez runs the shop. He's reserved, kind and a little old-fashioned, and he only ever calls you friend. He stocks everything from coffee to fishing rods to seeds, buys your fish, crops and Goods, and sets out one collectible a week. He doesn't talk about Mr. Glaz. Spend enough at his counter and he'll remember you: his loyalty card goes from Stranger to Family, and Family gets the back room. See Main Street . Where: r!shop , r!sellfish , r!sellcrops . Chuck Alfrey Chuck runs the Bait & Tackle down at the docks: an old fisherman in a yellow raincoat with a story for everything, and maybe a third of them are true. He's talkative, superstitious (never whistle on the pier), swears he once saw the White Whale, keeps the server's records in chalk, and talks to the fish. He and Marquez are old friends. He'll call you Greenhorn until you've filled a page of the Fishdex, then Deckhand, Skipper and finally Old Salt. He sells the rods, the Cooler and the Boat, and pays you when you finish a page of the Fishdex. Where: r!fish shop , or Chuck's on Main Street. TODD TODD is a monitor with opinions. He's the house at the Rend-Sino, the lender of last resort ( r!bailout ), the law when the Underground gets out of hand, and the one who drops into chat with a question and a pot of Polygons. Win ten in a row at his casino and he'll have you escorted out. Ask him to rate something with r!rate ; he'll do it badly. The server's first landmark is a statue of him. Mr. Glaz A red robe with the hood pulled over his face, and in its shadow a single white eye. Paranoid to the point of madness: he whispers, then snaps, counts things nobody else can see, and never says anyone's name. He only comes out at night. He keeps his rules. See the Underground .

title: City Hall
summary: Under New Management: weekly mayoral elections, who can run and vote, the mayor's powers (business, taxes, public works, decrees, appointments), the limits on them, impeachment and the city treasury.
text: Every server elects a mayor each week. The mayor has real power over the server's economy: they can stop a company from being crashed and swallowed, set taxes, fund public works, and issue decrees. Everything they do goes on a public record, and the server can vote them out. At a glance Elections Weekly Nominations Mon–Thu Voting Fri–Sun 9 PM ET Who can vote Anyone Who can run Active players Elections Nominations run Monday to Thursday: r!mayor run [slogan] . You can drop out with r!mayor withdraw . Voting runs Friday to Sunday at 9 PM Eastern: r!vote @player . Anyone with an account in the server can vote, once; you can change your vote until it closes. r!mayor race shows the ballot. Results come in Sunday at 9 PM Eastern. The winner is mayor until the next Sunday at 9 PM. A tie goes to whoever signed up first. If nobody runs, the seat stays empty for the week. Who can run: active players: you have to have played on at least ? different days in the last 7, with an account at least ? days old in the server. r!mayor eligible checks. Term limit: at most ? terms in a row; then sit one out before running again. The mayor's powers r!mayor help lists them in Discord. Every action needs a reason, and it goes on the public record ( r!mayor log ). Business Block a takeover bid or merger: r!mayor block PREY <reason> . A blocked bidder gets their premium back. Freeze a player company's trading for 24 hours: nobody can buy or sell its shares. ? a term. Investigate a player: their buys and sells in player companies go on the public record for ? days. Fine a company (from its treasury) or a player (from their wallet): up to ? , at most ? , ? a term. Fines go into the city treasury. Bail out a company with a grant from the city treasury, to save one that's being crashed. Taxes A sales tax on Marquez's shop (0 to ? ), a property tax on top of the building tax (0 to ? of a building's value a day), and a tax on casino winnings (0 to ? of what you win over your bet). r!mayor tax shop 5 . Changes start at midnight Eastern , so nobody gets ambushed. Taxes belong to the mayor's term: a new mayor starts at 0. Collections: the mayor sets Collect Call 's fee ( ? to ? ) and grace period ( ? to ? days). The fee goes to the city. Public works The mayor designs them: pick an effect, a size, how long, and a name, and the city treasury pays. r!mayor build rent 10 3 Main Street Repaving ; r!mayor quote rent 10 3 prices it first. One of each effect at a time. The cost is the rate × the size × the days × the server's active players (at least 5). Decrees and appointments Decrees: anything the mayor wants to say goes on the record ( r!mayor decree <text> ). Once a day a decree can also do something: Happy Hour for 2 hours, no heists for 24 hours, double dailies until midnight, a market holiday for player companies until midnight, or an amnesty (everyone's Heat drops by 25). Appointments: a Treasurer (funds public works and bailouts) and a Police Chief (investigates and freezes). r!mayor appoint chief @player . The limits The mayor and the appointees can never pay themselves , or anything they own, from the city treasury. Conflicts of interest: no business powers on a company they own, hold shares in, or are bidding on (or the company it's merging with). Everything goes on the public record , with a reason. Impeachment: r!impeach opens a 24-hour vote. If more than half as many players as voted in the last election vote yes (and at least ? ), the mayor is out; their taxes and decrees end, and the seat is empty until the next election. One impeachment vote a term. The city treasury Taxes, fines and collection fees go in; public works and bailouts come out. It's public: r!mayor shows the balance, the taxes, what's being built and the latest entries on the record. Unspent money stays for the next mayor.

title: The City
summary: Building on your server's 8×8 map: the twelve buildings, levels, neighbors, tax, freight and train robberies, landmarks, squatters, bids and condemnation.
text: Every server has one map: an 8×8 grid of open land, A1 to H8. Anyone can claim a tile and build on it. Buildings pay rent every day, cost upkeep, wear down, and change the tiles around them. Nobody is capped, but property tax climbs with every building you own, rivals can bid to buy you out, and a place you neglect gets squatters before it falls apart. At a glance Map 8×8, per server Land ⬡1,000 a tile Cheapest building Shack, ⬡2,500 Levels up to 3 Tax-free 1 to 3 buildings TIP A good first building: a Shack next to someone's Park. The Park adds 15% to its rent. See the live map on the city page . Building and upgrading Pick an empty tile and a building: r!property build C4 shack (or just r!build C4 shack ). You pay the building's price plus the land, and construction takes real time; no rent until it's done. Most buildings can be upgraded twice ( r!property upgrade C4 ): rent goes ×1.6, then ×2.4, and the building is fixed up to 100% along the way. Selling or tearing down Sell ( r!property sell C4 ): the bank buys the building and the land for ? of everything that went into it (less if it's run down), and the tile is open land again. Tear down ( r!property teardown C4 park ): knock it down and build something else, keeping the land. The crew pays ? of what went in as salvage, and you pay the new building's price (no land this time). The twelve buildings FROM THE BOT A Lighthouse has to go on the edge of the map, and one Barn is all a farm needs. Neighbors This Shack earns 100% + 15% (Park) − 15% (Factory) + 10% (Station) = 110% rent. "Next door" means the eight tiles around a building, diagonals included. Park next door: +15% rent (up to two Parks). Factory next door: −15% rent and faster wear. Stations, Factories and Warehouses don't mind the smoke. Station within two tiles: +10% rent. Corner Shop: +5% for each home beside it (Shacks, Apartments, Mansions), up to four. Police Station next door: no squatters, and Mr. Glaz won't set up within a tile of it. Rent, upkeep and tax Each building pays its rent once a day, scaled by its level, its condition and its neighbors, and charges its upkeep plus property tax on its value. Buildings lose about 2% condition a day (more in storms, next to a Factory, or when you can't pay); repair with r!property repair all . A Lighthouse halves storm damage to all your buildings. What each building does Ballroom: a Mansion owner can throw a party once a day ( r!property party ): chat pay doubles for everyone in the server for an hour. Storefront: pick a player company for your Corner Shop ( r!property storefront C4 TICK ); it earns 10% of the shop's rent, paid by the Reserve. Corner Shops also launder hot loot. Production: a Factory makes 24 crates of Goods a day per level. Sell them to Marquez ( r!property goods sell ) or ship them by freight for more. More Land: a Barn unlocks six more farm plots. Branch Manager: a Bank Branch adds 25% per level to the interest on your savings. Cold Storage: a Warehouse sells your crops at the best price of the last few days. Wholesale: a Warehouse orders seeds straight from the supplier with r!property wholesale polyfruit 3 : ? over Marquez's price, never touching his shelf, with your own daily allowance of each seed ( ? / ? / ? by Warehouse level; Polygon Fruit ? / ? / ? ). Allowances reset at midnight Eastern. Freight and train robberies Own a finished Station and you can ship your whole crop basket and your Goods by train, once every 6 hours: crops at 15% over market, Goods at ⬡30 a crate. The train takes half an hour. While it's on the rails, any crew can rob it with r!heist train and take up to half of what it carries. Landmarks Build It and They Will Come: the whole server funds landmarks together, one after another, with r!landmark donate <amount> . Donations go into the Reserve, and every finished landmark gives everyone here a perk. The top donor on each one gets Foreman . Squatters, bids and condemnation Squatters: below 40%, squatters can move in. No rent until you evict them ( r!property evict C4 , three days of rent) or repair to 75%. Condemned: at 0% the bank takes the place (paying you a tenth of its value) and auctions it for a day. If nobody bids, it's torn down. Buyout bids: anyone can bid at least 25% over a building's value ( r!property bid C4 <amount> ). The owner has a day to accept or refuse; refusing costs 15% of the bid and shields the building for a week. No answer, and it's sold. Selling: the bank buys any building back for up to 80% of what went into it (less if it's run down) and tears it down.

title: Commands
summary: Every Render Vision command, by section, with its aliases and slash form. Filter by name or what it does.
text: Every command works as r!command or as a slash command. Words in <angle brackets> are needed; words in [square brackets] are optional. Moderator commands share one slash command, /mod . Press / anywhere on the wiki to search. Every command FROM THE BOT

title: Player companies
summary: Found your own company, grow it level by level, take it public on the exchange, pay yourself, and defend it from hostile takeovers.
text: Any player can found a company. It has a treasury, levels up as you invest, and at level 3 it can go public: other players can buy its shares, and it gets its own page on the exchange . At a glance Founding ⬡2,500, approved by mods Go public at level 3 Listing fee ⬡2,000 Shares 1,000 ( 400 for sale) Founding one r!found TICK Your Company Name sends it to the server's moderators for approval; if the name is rejected you get your money back. Once approved, that money becomes the company's treasury. See it with r!company . The treasury grows when you invest ( r!invest ), when players work there (every shift adds half the worker's pay, and anyone can r!apply TICK ), and from share sales after it goes public. Levels Upgrades are paid from the treasury ( r!upgrade ). Every level costs upkeep each day, and raises what the company can pay. Going public At level 3 (Firm), r!ipo lists the company. Anyone but the owner can then buy and sell its shares, and the first 400 shares sold fund the company. Its price moves with trading, and its treasury earns from revenue: farmers' market sales, a Corner Shop's Storefront on the city map, and more. Once it's public, your employees' pay follows the share price like a house company's: double the IPO price and shifts pay double, from ? × up to ? × the normal pay. You can pay yourself a salary of up to 10% of the treasury a day ( r!salary ), but the stock dips when you do. Upkeep and closing The treasury pays upkeep every day. Miss a payment and the market panics; keep missing them and the price slides to zero and the company closes for good, taking every share with it. A private company closes after missing upkeep three days in a row. Closing it yourself r!closecompany shows what you'd get; r!closecompany confirm does it. A public company first buys out every shareholder at the share price, from the treasury and then your wallet if the treasury runs short. You get what's left of the treasury minus a ? closing fee. The levels you paid for are gone, employees lose their jobs, and you can't found another company for ? days. Selling it r!sellcompany @player <price> offers the whole company (treasury, level and staff) to another player in your server. They have a day to answer with r!sellcompany accept or decline ; r!sellcompany cancel takes it back. The buyer can't already run a company, and has to sell any shares they hold in it first. No sale while a takeover bid is open. NPC workers A company can hire staff who earn for its treasury every day, even when nobody's playing. r!company staff lists them; r!company hire hires one for ? from the treasury. How many: ? at Startup, ? at Small Business, ? at Firm, ? at Corporation and up. Wages: paid from the treasury every day. The going rate is ? ; you can set anything from ? to ? with r!company wage <name|all> <amount> . What they earn: about ? a day each, times the company's level bonus, and more when they're happy (half as much at their unhappiest, half again at their happiest). Moods: pay at least the going rate and moods hold or rise (well above it, they rise fast). Underpay them, or let the treasury run dry, and moods fall. Under ? they may go on strike for a day (no work, no pay). At 0 they quit, and they tell you why. r!company fire <name> lets one go. Takeovers and mergers If someone is crashing your company to take it over cheap, go to City Hall : the mayor can block the bid, freeze trading, and fine or investigate whoever is behind it. Hostile takeover: a player who holds at least half of the shares for sale can bid for your company with r!takeover , putting up a premium of a quarter of its worth. You have a day to answer; no answer and it goes through. Poison pill: defend for a tenth of the company's worth ( r!takeover defend ). The bidder gets their premium back minus a 20% break fee, which goes to you, and your company is shielded from takeovers for 7 days. Merger: two owners can agree to merge with r!merge .

title: Emojis
summary: All of the bot's pixel-art emojis, by group, with their names.
text: The bot draws its own emojis: 128-pixel art on a 32-pixel grid, each in a frame with its section's color. They show up in the bot's replies and across the site. An item's emoji is named after the item. Every emoji FROM THE BOT

title: Events
summary: World events that change the game for an hour, what happens in December, and the birthday parties.
text: World events FROM THE BOT Every few hours, one of these runs for an hour in every server. r!event shows the one running now. December: Polygon Holidays The advent calendar ( r!advent ): a door a day from December 1 to 25. Missed doors open late. Polygons, seeds, items and collectibles, and something special behind the last door. Secret Santa ( r!santa ): sign up by December 14. On the 15th everyone who joined is matched up; wrap a gift of Polygons and an item, and it's delivered on Christmas Day. The holiday shelf: Marquez stocks December-only collectibles and paints. Snow Day: a December event with no work but double chat pay. In October, pumpkins sell for 25% more. Birthdays Two parties a year, in every server. r!birthday shows the party and your server's cake. The birthday page has the full list. RendConomy Big Birthday Blowout! November 9 to 15. RendConomy came to The Render Room on November 9, 2026, so the first one is in 2027. Render Vision's Big Birthday! August 17 to 19, the developer's birthday. Birthday Bash (November 9 and August 18): chat pay x1.5 all day, and a ⬡250 bonus on every daily. The cake: every shift, gig, catch and harvest adds a piece to your server's cake. When it's full, everyone who helped is paid (⬡1,000 on RendConomy's birthday, ⬡500 on Render Vision's). The Party shelf at Marquez's: Cake Slices (eat one for a little gift), a Party Hat (one per party), and on RendConomy's birthday a numbered Candle for the age it's turning. Everywhere else: cake on the Slots reels, more in every progressive jackpot, Chuck's Party Fish in any water (it isn't part of the Fishdex), and TODD's birthday questions. RendConomy's birthday only: the time capsule ( r!birthday capsule <one line> , opened with your name at the next birthday) and r!yearbook , your RendConomy so far.

title: Everyday money
summary: The daily allowance, chat pay, TODD's drop-ins, savings accounts, loans between players, gifts, trades, your inbox, profile and leaderboards.
text: The daily allowance r!daily pays ⬡250 once per day; the day turns over at midnight Eastern. Claim it every day to build a streak. Chat pay and drop-ins Talking in the server pays ⬡5 to ⬡15 a message, once a minute, up to ⬡300 a day. Very short messages don't count. Now and then TODD drops in with a question and a pot of Polygons for whoever answers first. A Mansion party, the Stadium landmark and the Gossip Hour event all raise chat pay. Savings Lock Polygons away and get them back with interest: r!savings deposit 1000 7 . Up to 3 accounts and ⬡50,000 in all, from ⬡100 each. A Bank Branch on the city map adds 25% per level to your interest. Loans From TODD: r!bailout when you're nearly broke: ⬡500 now, ⬡600 owed. No gambling until it's paid ( r!repay ). From another player: r!loan @player 1000 5 asks for ⬡1,000 at 5% a day (up to 25%); they accept or decline. Loans are due in a week. Overdue, and half of what you earn from work, dailies and dividends goes to the lender until it's paid. r!loans lists yours; a lender can r!forgive . Collections: ? days after the due date, the lender can run r!collect @borrower . TODD takes what's owed, plus a ? collection fee for the city treasury (the mayor can set it between 5% and 20%, and the grace period between 1 and 5 days), from the borrower's wallet, then their savings (closed early, no interest), their shares at the market price, then their shop items at Marquez's buy-back price. Never buildings, companies or collectibles. The lender only gets what they're owed. Borrowers get a DM when the loan goes overdue and again when it can be collected. Gifts and trades Gifts: r!gift @player 500 sends Polygons with a 5% fee, up to ⬡5,000 a day. Trades: offer Polygons and/or an item for someone else's ( r!trade @player 500 for rod ). What you offer is held safely until they answer; offers expire in a day (you get it back), and you can have three open. Your inbox r!inbox collects what happened while you were away: receipts, price alerts, bids on your buildings, ready crops, trade offers. On the site, the bell in the top bar shows new ones. r!receipts on also sends receipts by DM. Profile and leaderboards A Title item sets the line under your name ( r!settitle ); r!settitle clear removes it. r!profile shows your net worth, achievements and pinned showcase ( r!showcase ). Customize its color, theme, banner and frame, or edit it on your profile page on the site. r!leaderboard ranks the server by net worth, Polygons or shifts. Playing from the site Log in with Discord on the Play hub to work, farm, build, trade and read your inbox from a browser, and open the Trading Floor Activity right inside Discord.

title: Farming
summary: Seeds, planting, watering and harvesting; crop grades and daily prices; mutations; more plots and the Barn; Fertilizer; and the farmhand.
text: Every server gives you a small farm. Buy seeds from Marquez (or order them wholesale, if you own a Warehouse ), plant them, water them once per stage, and harvest when they're ready. Crops grow in real time, even while you're away. Sell your basket to Marquez, at the farmers' market, or by freight . At a glance Plots 3 to start, up to 15 Wilts after 12 thirsty hours Farmhand ⬡150 a day Crops r!plant carrot fills every empty plot (or r!plant corn 2 for just plot 2); then r!water and r!harvest . Tomatoes keep producing: after the first harvest they regrow twice, in half the time. Pumpkins are worth 25% more in October. TIP Crows can eat a crop (a Scarecrow keeps them off), and Storm events can flatten crops outside a Greenhouse. Rain waters everything for free. Quality grades Every crop is graded the moment it's harvested. Its grade sets the range its price is rolled from when you sell it: each one is rolled separately, so a basket of the same crop sells for a little more or less every time. Harvest a Prime crop for Quality Control , and a Prime crop that's also Golden or Rainbow for Cream of the Crop . Daily prices On top of grades, every crop's price moves each day, between 80% and 120% of normal, the same for everyone. r!farm prices shows today's. A Warehouse on the city map lets you sell at the best price of the last 3 days (5 at level 2, 7 at level 3). Mutations Now and then a crop comes out special, and worth far more: Selling To Marquez: r!sellcrops sells your whole basket. At the farmers' market: r!sellcrops TICK sells to a player company for 10% more, and the company earns a cut (not your own company). By freight: with a Station on the city map, ship the basket for 15% over market. See freight . More plots and the Barn Buy plots one at a time with r!buyplot . Past nine, you need a Barn on the city map , which unlocks six more. The farm always shows three rows: three plots across, or five with a Barn. Fertilizer Fertilizer makes a crop grow 50% faster and come out Prime more often. r!fertilize works it into every growing crop at once, as far as your Fertilizer goes, or r!fertilize 3 for one plot. Buy it from Marquez or make it from fishing junk with r!compost . The farmhand Hire him with r!farmhand hire for ⬡150 a day. While you're away he waters everything, harvests each crop the moment it's ready, and replants from his seed shed (the same crop as before, or what he has most of). He never buys seeds: stock his shed with r!farmhand give carrot 20 . Give him Fertilizer too ( r!farmhand give fertilizer 10 ) and he works one into every crop he plants. When you open your farm, he tells you what he did while you were gone. He DMs you when he runs out of seeds (turn that off with r!farmhand dms off ). If you can't pay him, he quits and leaves the shed with you. He doesn't sell your crops; that's still your call.

title: Render's File Tycoon
summary: The site's pipeline game: wire network gear, downloaders, processors and markets into a file pipeline, sell to the Rend-Conomy companies at live prices, upgrade your PC, and cash out into your RendConomy wallet.
text: Render's File Tycoon is a pipeline builder in your browser. Drag modules onto the board, wire them together, and turn downloaded files into Polygons. Prices follow the real Rend-Conomy market, and once you're logged in, what you earn can go into your RendConomy wallet. At a glance Where /games/rft/ Saves In your browser Cash out ⬡5 per ⬡1,000 Daily cap ⬡500 Building a pipeline Network modules (from WiFi up to fiber) give you bandwidth. Everything downstream shares it. Downloaders pull one kind of file: Documents, Ebooks, Images, Audio, Archives, Video, Software or Databases. Bigger files are worth more and take longer. Processors (scanner, antivirus, compressor, decoder, metadata tagger, encryptor) make files worth more, but use CPU and heat. Upload & sell : an uploader and a market (basic, premium, auction, seeder, mirror) turn files into Polygons. Storage and utilities (caches, buffers, splitters, sorters, schedulers) keep things flowing. Drag from a port to wire two modules. Hover a module and press U to upgrade it, D to delete it. Middle-drag or hold Space to pan, scroll to zoom. The 3D view shows the same board in 3D. Your PC Everything runs on your PC, and its limits are real. Hardware Upgrades raise them: the CPU (how much processing you can run), RAM (buffers and parallel downloads), storage (disk space), the network card (bandwidth) and the cooler (heat; running hot throttles everything). The last tier of each is a joke price. Somebody will buy The Gregulator anyway. The market Each file type sells to one company, and pays more when that company's stock is up: BNW buys Documents and Databases, BLU Software and Archives, RRM Video and Audio, NACH Images and Ebooks. The sidebar's Market demand shows the live multipliers. The RendConomy wallet Log in with Discord (the button in the sidebar) and you can cash out : ⬡5 into your RendConomy wallet for every ⬡1,000 you've earned in the game, up to ⬡500 a day, paid from the Reserve. The bot remembers what it already paid, so the same earnings never pay twice. The rest keeps until tomorrow. Six achievements unlock in the bot too: First Byte, Six Figures, The Gregulator, Fresh Install, Contractor, and a secret one. The Terminal The Terminal takes codes. Some are out there, if you know where to listen.

title: Your first day
summary: Join, claim a daily, work a shift, and what Polygons are. Everything a new player needs in the first ten minutes.
text: The Rend-Conomy is the economy game inside Render Vision, the Render Productions Discord bot. You earn Polygons (written ⬡), spend them, invest them, and occasionally lose them in spectacular ways. Every server has its own economy: your balance in one server has nothing to do with another. Your achievements follow you everywhere. At a glance You start with ⬡500 Daily allowance ⬡250 Resets 12 AM Eastern Prefix r! or / Joining There's nothing to sign up for. The first command you use creates your account with ⬡500 . Every command works as r!command or as a slash command ( /command ); r!help lists them by section, and the commands page lists every one. Your first ten minutes Claim your daily: r!daily pays ⬡250 once per day (Eastern time). Keep a streak going for the achievements. Get a job: r!apply RRM (or NACH, BLU, BNW, BSTG). Then r!work every 15 minutes. Each shift gives you a quick task; type the answer in the channel. See Work . Do a gig between shifts: r!gig needs no job and works every 10 minutes. r!oddjob gives you up to 10 more small jobs a day. Look around the shop: r!shop opens Main Street: Marquez's shelves, Chuck Alfrey's tackle and players' stores. A Bamboo Rod or some seeds are good first buys. Check your money: r!bal shows everything you have, what you owe, and your net worth. TIP Just talking in the server earns Polygons too: a few for each message (one a minute counts), up to ⬡300 a day. Spamming doesn't help. Where Polygons come from Almost every payout in the game, from shifts to rent to casino wins, is paid out of the Polygon Reserve , a single pot shared by everyone. Almost everything you spend goes back into it. That's worth understanding early, because it's the reason payouts can shrink. If you go broke TODD will lend you ⬡500 with r!bailout when you have less than ⬡100 , and you'll owe him ⬡600 . While you owe TODD, the Rend-Sino won't let you gamble. Pay him back with r!repay . Where to go next Read about the Reserve , then pick a path . Achievements are a great guide to what's possible: r!achievements shows yours, and every one pays out the first time.

title: Fishing
summary: The Fishy Deep: six places to fish, rods and gear from Chuck Alfrey, bait and worms, reeling in the big ones, weights and giants, the Fishdex, server records, trophies, the Saturday tournament, and what everything is worth.
text: Get a rod and cast with r!fish . Pick a place ( r!fish river ) and a bait ( r!fish river worm ). You might catch nothing, snag your line, pull up junk, a lost wallet, a treasure chest or a message in a bottle, or a fish. Medium and bigger fish fight back: you reel them in with buttons. Every fish has its own weight, and heavier is worth more. At a glance Cast every 3 min Bait ⬡5 Bag holds 50 ( 100 with a Cooler) Places 6 Fish 34 kinds Where to fish r!fish places shows which ones you can reach. The Lake is the default. The Sewer is open to anyone, but every cast there adds 3 Heat (see the Underground ). Ice fishing only opens in December. Gear: Chuck Alfrey's Bait & Tackle Chuck Alfrey has it all on Main Street : the Bamboo Rod and Lures, and everything better. r!fish shop , then r!fish buy carbon . Each rod tier also means fewer empty casts, bigger fish more often, and a line that holds more tension. Bait Plain bait costs ? a cast (free with a Shack's Bait Shed). A Lure (from Chuck) lasts ? casts and brings bigger fish. Worms are free: r!farm compost turns each piece of junk into ? worms (and Fertilizer). Small and medium fish love them. r!fish worm . Carrots from your farm work the same way. A fish as bait brings out the next size up: r!fish perch uses your lightest Perch. The odds of a cast with plain bait and a Bamboo Rod, at midday in calm weather: Better rods, lures, worms, rain (fewer empty casts), storms (more legends) and the mayor's fishing luck public work all shift these. Reeling in Small fish come straight in. Anything bigger is a fight: a Line in bar, a Tension bar, and two buttons. Reel pulls it closer, but raises the tension. Let out eases the tension, but gives a little line back. Every round, the fish pulls (tension jumps), runs (it takes line) or rests . Tension past what your rod can hold and the line snaps . Line in to 100% and it's yours. Let it get away, or take longer than 60 seconds, and it's gone. Bigger fish fight harder, and legends hardest of all. Better rods hold more tension. Every catch A fish's worth scales with its weight. Prices also change every day (80–120%, the same for everyone), so the same fish sells for more on a good day. Weights, giants and records Every fish rolls a weight in its range, leaning to the middle. ? of small, medium and large fish are giants : ? to ? times the normal weight, and they fight a bit harder. Server records: the heaviest of each fish anyone has caught here. r!fish records . Trophies: r!fish mount pike puts your heaviest Pike on your profile (it comes out of your bag, so you can't sell it). The Fishdex r!fish dex lists every fish by place, with a silhouette until you catch one and your heaviest after. Finishing a place's page pays a reward from Chuck Alfrey (in the table above). Catch every fish there is for Gotta Catch 'Em All! The Saturday tournament Every Saturday (Eastern time), enter with r!fish tournament join for ? . Your heaviest single fish that day counts. At midnight the Reserve adds ? to the entries, and the top 3 split the pot 60 / 30 / 10. r!fish tournament shows the standings. Selling r!fish sell sells your whole bag at today's prices. Junk sells for a little, or compost it. Own a Warehouse and your fish stay fresh: they sell at the best price of the last 3, 5 or 7 days, by level. Treasure chests pay out Polygons or a useful item; messages in bottles pay nothing, but they say things. Perks and events A Shack gives you free bait (Bait Shed). A Lighthouse makes plain bait fish like a Lure (Beacon), and opens the Pier without a Carbon Rod. The Fish Frenzy event lets you cast every 90 seconds, and plain bait works like a Lure. The mayor can fund a fishing luck public work: fewer empty casts and bigger fish for everyone.

title: Glossary
summary: Short definitions of the words the Rend-Conomy uses: Heat, escrow, the payout factor, net worth and more.
text: Terms Polygons (⬡) The currency. Every server has its own Polygons. The Reserve The house's pot of Polygons: almost every payout comes from it and most spending goes back in. More . Payout factor The share of a payout that's actually paid. 100% normally; lower when the Reserve is under a quarter full. Net worth Everything you have: Polygons, savings, shares, buildings, minus what you owe. Escrow Polygons held safely by the bot while something is undecided, like a bid or a trade. You get them back if it falls through. Shift One round of work at your job: a task, then pay. Every 15 minutes. Rush A bonus task right after a shift, which only pays if you get it right. Dividends What shares earn while you hold them. Short A bet that a stock will fall. Limit / stop order An order to buy or sell automatically when a price is reached. Grade A crop's quality: Poor, Fine or Prime. It sets the range its price is rolled from. Mutation A rare crop that comes out Golden, Rainbow or Square and is worth many times more. Tile One square of a server's 8×8 city map, named like C4. Condition How well kept a building is, 0–100%. Rent scales with it. Squatters People living in a neglected building. No rent until they're gone. Condemned A building that fell to 0%. The bank takes it and auctions it. Freight Shipping your crops and Goods by train from your Station. Goods Crates a Factory makes. Sell them to Marquez or ship them. Landmark A big building the whole server funds together, with a perk for everyone. VIP Your Rend-Sino level, from everything you've ever bet. Comes with a daily free spin. Progressive jackpot A pot every bet in the server adds to. Three diamonds on Slots win it. Heat How much attention you've drawn from TODD, 0–100 (five stars). High Heat gets you raided. Contraband What Mr. Glaz sells: items that bend the rules. Hot loot Stolen valuables from heists. Fence or launder them before they get you caught. World event A change that runs for an hour in every server, like Happy Hour or a Storm.

title: Heists
summary: Plan a heist with a crew of three to five: targets, roles and their odds, stakes, hauls, fines, and robbing freight trains.
text: Someone plans a heist in a channel, others join with a role, and when the leader starts it everyone pays a stake. Then it plays out. A clean job splits the haul evenly; a failed one loses the stakes, and if TODD catches the crew, there's a fine on top. At a glance Crew 3 to 5 Per player one every 6 hours Per server one an hour Targets r!heist vault , stash , reserve or train . Hauls come out of the Reserve, so robbing it really does hurt everyone. Roles Pick a role when you join. Each one adds to the crew's odds: Robbing a train When a Station owner ships freight on the city map , the train spends half an hour on open track. A crew can rob it in that window and take up to half of what it carries. The owner still gets the rest when it arrives. You can't rob your own train. Hot loot A clean heist sometimes drops hot loot for each crew member: a ring, a painting, a gem or a crate. It's worth a lot, but holding it draws Heat. Fence it or launder it through the Underground . TIP A Lockpick Set adds 15% to your next heist, and the Police Strike event adds 15% for everyone for an hour.

title: Iso-Chess
summary: A roguelike chess march in 3D: three acts, enemies that show their next moves, power cards, a permadeath army, unlocks from Marquez's shop and Polygons for your runs.
text: Iso-Chess is chess as a roguelike, on a floating 3D board. March your army through three acts. The enemy shows its next moves, so you can dodge, block, or spend cards to turn the fight. Every piece you lose is gone for good. At a glance Where /games/chess/ Acts 3, each with a boss Saves In your browser Pays up to ⬡250 a day A run Three acts: the Rabble Fields, the Archers' Causeway and the Hollow Kingdom. Each is a map of battles, elites, camps and events, with a King at the end. Telegraphs: the enemy shows what it's about to do. Read it and play around it. Your army has names, and veterans earn traits. Lose a piece and it stays lost. Goals change by fight: take the king, rout them, survive, or escort a piece across. With the bot Openings and skins are sold on the Iso-Chess shelf at Marquez's ( r!shop chess ): the Gambit, the Fortress and the Cavalry, and Obsidian, Jade, Crimson and Frost pieces. Buy one and it's yours in the game, once you're logged in on the site. Polygons: a finished run pays into your wallet (⬡10 a battle, ⬡25 an elite, ⬡60 a boss, ⬡150 for winning it all), up to ⬡250 a day. Z and X tilt the camera.

title: Items
summary: Everything Marquez sells, by shelf, with prices, stock and what each item does, plus the weekly collectibles.
text: Each server has its own stock, filled by Marquez's delivery truck three times a day, and prices move with demand (see Main Street ). The prices below are list prices. One collectible is on sale each week, one per customer. Buy with r!shop buy <item> [amount] and use with r!use <item> [amount] ; items marked "works on its own" do their thing just by being in your inventory. Using lots at once: r!use mystery 10 or r!use mystery all opens up to ? in one message. Coffee, the Customizer Kit, the Megaphone, paints and the Rush Order go one at a time. Mystery: ? of the time it holds ? , ? an Overtime pass, and otherwise ⬡ ? – ? . On average that's about what it costs. Rush Order: r!use rush order coffee has Marquez restock that one item to full, for everyone in your server. Not for collectibles, and you keep the Rush Order if the item is already full. Selling back: r!shop sell <item> [amount|all] . Marquez pays ? of his list price and puts it back on his shelf. He doesn't buy collectibles (trade those with r!trade ), and fish and crops have their own buyers. Throwing away: r!discard <item> [amount|all] , for nothing. Every item FROM THE BOT

title: The market, Exchange and city map
summary: The live Rend-Conomy pages on the site: the market and each company's page, the Exchange of player companies (with trading), the city map, the bot's page and the patch notes.
heads: The bot and the patch notes
text: The Rend-Conomy pages update live from the bot, about every 30 seconds. The market The Rend-Conomy page shows every company's price, the market's status, the Reserve and the news. Each house company has its own page ( RRM , NACH , BLU , BNW , BSTG ) with a chart of the last week. Logged in, you can buy and sell right from the page. The Exchange The Exchange lists every player company: its ticker, founder, level, treasury and, once it's public, its share price. Each one has its own page with a trade box. The city map The city map shows each server's 8×8 grid: who built what, how it's holding up, the landmarks going up, and trains on the line. Click a tile for its details. The bot and the patch notes The bot's page has its live stats, every command, the shop and the whole emoji gallery. The patch notes list every update, newest first; the bot posts each one in Discord when it goes live.

title: Main Street
summary: Main Street: Marquez's delivery truck and each server's own stock, prices that move with demand, the daily deal, Black Friday every Friday, Marquez's loyalty card and back room, wishlists, Chuck Alfrey's Bait & Tackle, and player stores in Corner Shops.
heads: The daily deal and Black Friday
text: r!shop opens Main Street : Marquez's Shop, Chuck Alfrey's Bait & Tackle, the stores players run out of their Corner Shops, and the alley (at night). Each server has its own shelves, filled by Marquez's delivery truck. Prices move with what people buy, there's a deal every day and a sale every Friday, and the more you spend at Marquez's, the better he treats you. At a glance Deliveries 8 AM, 2 PM, 8 PM ET Daily deal 30% off Black Friday Every Friday Sells back for 40% Wishlist 5 items Shopping r!shop opens the street. Buttons take you to Marquez's, Chuck's, the player stores and your loyalty card. At Marquez's, pick a shelf from the dropdown and an item from the second one to look closer: its price (and why), how many are left, and Buy 1, Buy 5 or Buy max. By name: r!shop buy coffee 3 and r!shop sell coffee all . r!shop casino opens a shelf directly. Selling back: Marquez pays ? of his list price, whatever the sale. Buying on sale and selling back never pays. The delivery truck Every server has its own stock now, so one busy server can't empty the shelves for everyone. The truck comes at ? Eastern and fills every shelf back up. A few minutes later it pulls up in a busy channel to say so (in the drop-in channel, if your server set one). The weekly collectible still changes once a week. A Rush Order ( r!use rush order coffee ) still refills one item right away, for your server. Prices that move At each delivery, every regular item's price moves a little: Sold out since the last truck: + ? . Sold less than ? of the stock: − ? . Otherwise it drifts ? back toward normal. Prices stay between ? and ? of the list price. The shelf shows ▲ or ▼ when an item has moved. The Title, the Mystery box and collectibles never move and are never discounted. The daily deal and Black Friday Daily deal: one item a day is ? off. It's the same item in every server. Black Friday, every Friday (Eastern): one shelf is featured at ? off and everything else is ? off. The featured shelf changes each week, in this order: ? . Sales don't stack with each other (you get the bigger one), but your loyalty discount comes on top. Marquez's loyalty card Everything you spend at Marquez's counter in a server counts toward your card there ( r!shop card ). He warms up as you go. The back room: for Family, the rare items ( ? or fewer on the shelf) have as many again in the back, refilled with every delivery. When the shelf is empty, you buy from the back. Wishlists r!shop want coffee puts an item on your wishlist (up to ? ); the same again takes it off, and r!shop want clear empties it. When a delivery brings something on it, you get a DM. Good Friends hear ? minutes before everyone else, and before the truck announces itself. Buying the item takes it off your list. Chuck Alfrey's Bait & Tackle Chuck has the Bamboo Rod and Lures (restocked by the same truck) and the better gear: rods, the Cooler and the Boat. Open it from Main Street or with r!fish shop , and buy with the buttons or r!fish buy carbon . See Fishing . Chuck doesn't care what you spend; he cares what you've caught. He calls you a Greenhorn until you finish a page of the Fishdex, a Deckhand after one, a Skipper after three, and an Old Salt once it's all done. Player stores Every finished Corner Shop on the map is a store. Stock it from your inventory and set your own price. There's no cap: if you want to beat Marquez, you'll have to be smart about it. r!shop stock coffee 3 at 150 puts 3 Coffee on your shelf at ⬡150 each. Add on C4 to pick which Corner Shop. Stocking an item you already sell adds to it and sets the new price. r!shop unstock coffee (or unstock coffee 2 ) takes them back. r!shop store shows your shelves. Slots per Corner Shop by level: ? . Anything in your inventory can go on a shelf: Marquez's items, collectibles, crops, Goods. Fish stay in the fishing bag. Buyers find you on Main Street, or go straight there with r!shop @you (and r!shop @you coffee 2 buys). They pay your price plus the mayor's sales tax, and you keep the whole price. Every sale sends you a receipt. A Corner Shop under ? % condition, or with squatters, closes until it's fixed. If the building is sold, torn down or condemned, everything on its shelves comes back to your inventory.

title: The daily deal and Black Friday
The Market
summary: Shares in the five house companies: buying and selling, dividends, limit and stop orders, brokers and short selling.
text: Five house companies trade on the Rend-Conomy market, and their prices move all day on their own. Buy shares, hold them for dividends, sell them higher, or bet against them. Prices are the same in every server; your shares belong to the server you bought them in. Starting prices RRM · Render Room ⬡167 NACH · De Nacho ⬡120 BNW · Business Numbers Working ⬡80 BSTG · Bastardly Glory ⬡75 BLU · Builder's League United ⬡47 Trading hours You can trade from 3 AM to 9 PM Eastern , every day. Overnight the market is after hours: prices still drift (a quarter as much), but nobody can buy or sell, and orders and brokers wait for the open. Now and then TODD halts trading on a company or the whole market after a big move. Buying and selling r!market shows every price; r!chart RRM draws the last day; r!compare puts them side by side. Buy with r!buy RRM 10 (or an amount of Polygons) and sell with r!sell RRM all . Big trades move the price against you a little. The live prices are also on the Rend-Conomy page . Bastardly Glory is the wild one: it can soar, and it can crash. Goals and news Companies announce goals in the market news. Hit the goal and the stock jumps; miss it and it drops, and nobody knows the result ahead of time. Watch for breaking news, rumors that may or may not be true, and the odd story that shakes the whole market at once. Every company has good stretches and bad ones, and no stretch lasts forever. The Rend Times from Marquez's shop drops vague hints. Dividends Companies pay dividends per share as they do well. Every share you hold earns its part while you hold it; collect what's built up with r!dividends . Limit and stop orders Orders fill on their own while you're away ( r!order ): Limit buy: buy a number of shares once the price falls to your limit. The money is set aside until it fills. Limit sell: sell once the price rises to your target. Stop: sell once the price falls to your stop, to cut a loss. Up to 10 open at once; they expire after 7 days. Brokers A broker trades for you by rules you set ( r!broker ), for a daily salary and a cut of the profit. Each has a style: Short selling Think a stock will fall? r!short BSTG 20 bets on it: you profit by however much it drops, and lose by however much it rises. Opening one holds half its value as margin, plus a 1% fee, and you can short up to 100 shares of a company. If your loss reaches 90% of the margin, the short is closed for you. r!cover closes one. If a company goes bankrupt, every short on it pays out in full. TIP The Bear Rumors and Fire Sale events make shorts free to open for an hour.

title: The odds
summary: Every Rend-Sino game's payouts and expected return, the jackpot, VIP levels, and the odds of heists and fishing.
text: Every number here comes straight from the code, so it's exactly what the games do. "Expected return" is what a game pays back on average for every ⬡100 bet: 96% means you lose ⬡4 per ⬡100 over the long run. Rend-Sino games FROM THE BOT VIP levels Heists The base odds of each target; each role in the crew adds its bonus on top. Fishing Crop grades and mutations

title: Picking a path
summary: Trader, farmer, landlord, gambler or crook: what each way of playing is like, what it costs to start and where to read more.
text: There's no class to pick and you can do everything at once. But most players lean one way. Here's what each path feels like, roughly from the safest to the wildest. The worker Shifts every 15 minutes, gigs every 10, odd jobs and promotions. Steady, needs you to be around, and the pay follows your company's share price. Start: r!apply . Work → The farmer Buy seeds, plant, water, harvest, sell. Crops grow in real time from 30 minutes to a day, come out Poor, Fine or Prime, and sometimes mutate into something worth five or twelve times as much. Hire a farmhand and it runs while you're away. Start: seeds from r!shop garden , then r!farm . Farming → The angler A Fishing Rod and a few Polygons of bait per cast. Small fish make good bait for bigger ones, and somewhere out there is the White Whale. Start: a Rod from r!shop tackle , then r!fish . Fishing → The trader Buy and sell shares in the five house companies (and players' companies), collect dividends, set limit and stop orders, hire a broker, or short a stock you think will fall. Start: r!market . The Market → · Player companies → The landlord Claim tiles on your server's city map and build: Shacks, shops, Stations, Factories, Mansions. Rent comes in daily; upkeep, tax, neighbors and rivals' buyout bids keep it interesting. Start: ⬡1,000 of land plus a building. The City → The gambler The Rend-Sino: slots, blackjack, roulette, the Rocket and more, a progressive jackpot, and VIP levels with a free spin a day. Every game's odds are published, and win ten in a row and TODD throws you out. The Rend-Sino → The crook Heists with a crew, and at night, Mr. Glaz's black market: contraband, hot loot, smuggling and snitching. Every shady move adds Heat, and Heat gets you raided. Heists → · The Underground →

title: The Play hub
summary: Play Rend-Conomy from the site: your desk, Main Street, your farm, the city, odd jobs, trades and your inbox, plus the bell on every page.
text: The Play hub is Rend-Conomy in your browser. Log in with Discord, pick a server you play in, and everything you do runs through the bot as you, exactly like a command in chat. The tabs Desk: your balance, the daily, dividends, savings, loans, your history and your showcase. Main Street: Marquez's, Chuck's and the player stores, and your inventory. Farm: plant, water, harvest, sell, fertilize and compost, buy plots, and run your farmhand. City: your buildings on the map, building and upgrading, freight, Goods and the landmark. Odd Jobs , Trades and your Inbox . The server picker at the top decides where your actions go. A live price strip runs along the top. The bell Logged in, a bell sits in the top bar of every page. It lights up when something lands in your inbox (receipts, trade offers, reports, ready crops) and opens it. Logging in Log in with Discord only tells the site your Discord name and picture. It never sees your password or your messages. See the privacy policy for exactly what happens.

title: Profiles and the customizer
summary: Your public profile on the site: what's on it, the customizer (colors, themes, banners, frames, paints, pins), the share card, Settings, hiding your profile, and Linked Roles.
text: Every player has a public profile on the profile page : their achievements, collectibles, title, net worth, job and best Rend-Sino hit, across every server they play in. Making it yours Open your own profile while logged in and you can change its look right there: An accent color (any color once you've used a Customizer Kit from Marquez's), a theme , a banner and a frame . The crown banner and the glowing frame are for players with a legendary or mythic achievement. Paints from Marquez's Profile shelf (Holographic, TODD Terminal, Sunset, Void, Gold Rush, and the December ones). Try one on before you save. Pins: show off up to three achievements, and pin a collectible. In Discord, r!profile shows the same card. r!profile @player shows someone else's. The share card The Share button makes a big image of your profile in its own style, to copy or download. Other players On someone else's profile you can send them Polygons or offer a trade. Hiding your profile r!profile private takes yours off the site within a few minutes; r!profile private off brings it back. Settings The Settings tab works without logging in: switch off pop-ups, the peeking faces, holiday effects, shakes and glitches, or the pixel emojis. See Render Face . Linked Roles Servers can hand out roles from your real Rend-Conomy stats (Server Settings → Roles → Links → RendConomy): your net worth, achievement count, buildings, whether you founded a company, and days played, each from your best server. Link it once and the bot keeps it up to date.

title: The Rend-Sino
summary: Every Rend-Sino game, the progressive jackpot, VIP levels and free spins, the multiplayer blackjack table, Happy Hour and TODD's hot-streak rule.
text: TODD's casino. Every game's odds are published and match the code exactly ( the odds ), the house keeps a small, honest edge, and wins are paid from the Reserve . Bets start at ⬡10 . At a glance Minimum bet ⬡10 Jackpot starts at ⬡10,000 Hot-streak limit 10 wins VIP levels 5 The games Plus three that work differently: Ride the Bus ( r!bus ): four card guesses in a row, cash out any time after the first. The Polygon Derby ( r!derby ): start a race, everyone in the channel bets on a horse, and it runs live. The lottery ( r!lottery ): tickets are ⬡50 (up to 20 a week), and the pot is drawn every Sunday at 8 PM Eastern. Lose a spin on Slots and you get Redeem yourself : one free spin of 15 reels, and seven of a kind wins your bet back. The progressive jackpot Every bet in the server adds 1% to the jackpot ( 3% during Happy Hour). Three 💎 on Slots win it: all of it at the maximum Slots bet, a share of it below (bet half the max, win half the jackpot). Then it starts over from ⬡10,000 . r!jackpot shows how big it is. VIP and free spins VIP levels come from everything you've ever bet in the server. Each level comes with a free Slots spin every day ( r!vip spin ): win and it's paid, lose and it cost nothing. Free spins can hit the jackpot too. The blackjack table r!table 100 opens a table in the channel. Up to five players press Sit down , the host presses Deal , and everyone pays the stake. Hands are played in turn with Hit, Stand and Double; each player has 45 seconds before TODD stands for them. Then TODD plays his hand and every seat is paid like solo blackjack. Win at a table of three or more for House Party . Happy Hour A world event that comes around now and then: the jackpot grows three times as fast, VIPs get a second free spin, and TODD looks the other way on hot streaks. TODD's rules Hot streaks: win 10 games in a row and TODD has you escorted out for 3 hours. A Fake ID from Mr. Glaz gets you back in. No gambling while you owe TODD for a bailout. A game left unfinished for two minutes is forfeited. One moment between games. LOADED DICE Mr. Glaz sells Loaded Dice that improve your odds for a few games. TODD sometimes notices. See the Underground .

title: Render Face
summary: The robot head that watches your pointer, the little ones that peek in from the edges of the site, and the pop-ups, and how to turn them off.
text: Render Face is a big robot head with a screen for a face. Its eyes follow your pointer and it blinks now and then. It has opinions about what you do with that pointer. The face It frowns when your pointer leaves the window. It gets annoyed if you keep clicking it, and dizzy if you circle it. Little alert windows pop up from time to time. Press Escape to close the newest one. Around the site Its little ones peek in from the edges of other pages and run when you get close. Catch one before it escapes and it's deleted, into ones and zeros. The face keeps count. Pop-ups show up across the site too, in one of three looks (pixel, Win95 or CRT). Every one of them has a Make it stop link. Turning it off The Settings tab on your profile page (no login needed) switches off pop-ups, their sounds, the peeking faces, the tab titles that beg you to come back, the holiday lights and snow, shakes and glitches, and the pixel emojis. It also picks the pop-up style.

title: Render Productions
summary: Who makes all this, The Render Room on Discord, how updates and patch notes work, how to report a bug, and the wiki's Featured page.
text: Render Productions is an indie dev hub for The Render Room on Discord, run by friends who may or may not know what they're doing. It's owned by Chace "Render Vision" Page. Everything here, the bot, the games and the site, is made for that community. The Render Room The Render Room is where it all happens: the bot lives there, updates are announced there, and that's where to find the team. Join it from the Discord page . Updates and patch notes Updates come often. Each one gets a name and a patch note; Quick Adds are small ones and Hotfixes fix something. The patch notes list them all, and the bot posts each one in Discord when it goes live. Player ideas make it in all the time. Found a bug? Tell a moderator in The Render Room. Please don't use it to get ahead: the terms ask you to report bugs instead of exploiting them. The Featured page The wiki's home page features one page a week, and the players pick it: r!wiki vote <page> in Discord (once a week, across every server). The most votes this week wins next week. r!wiki shows the race. The fine print The terms of service and the privacy policy cover the bot and the site.

title: The Polygon Reserve
summary: The single pot every payout comes from and most spending goes back to, and why payouts shrink when it runs low.
text: The Polygon Reserve is the house's money. Shifts, gigs, rent, dividends, fish sales, casino wins and achievement payouts all come out of it. Shop purchases, bets, upkeep, fees and fines go back in. It's shared by every server, so how everyone plays affects everyone. At a glance Full size ⬡25,000,000 Payouts shrink below 25% Lowest payouts 10% When payouts shrink While the Reserve holds more than a quarter of its full size, every payout is paid in full. Below that, payouts shrink in step with it: at an eighth full, you get half; they never drop below a tenth. Your r!bal and most payout messages say when this is happening, and r!reserve shows exactly how full it is. WHY A shrinking payout is the economy's brake: it stops the house from paying out money it doesn't have. Helping it Spending puts Polygons back: the shop, upkeep, bets, the farmhand's wage. Donations: r!reserve donate <amount> . The top five patrons are listed in r!reserve , and there are achievements for it. Landmarks: money donated to a landmark goes into the Reserve too. Hurting it A heist on the Reserve takes straight from it, so robbing it really does cost everyone. Big casino wins and achievement payouts drain it too, which is why every game's odds are published and fair rather than generous.

title: Stationfall
summary: Survival on an asteroid: mine and smelt, build and pressurize a station, keep the air on, take in survivors and give them jobs, and hold out against the scrapper drones.
text: Stationfall : your ship broke apart over an asteroid field. You and your crewmate Ade made it down with a shelter kit. Mine the rock, smelt it into bars, build out the station, keep the air on, take in survivors, and hold out when the scrapper drones come at night. At a glance Where /games/stationfall/ Status Alpha Controls Keyboard and mouse Saves In your browser Controls WASD to move, click to use what you're holding, E to interact, B to build, I for your inventory. The top row of the inventory is your hotbar (keys 1–6). Staying alive Watch your health, oxygen, food and stamina . Outside a sealed room the air runs out fast. A space suit stretches it. Mine rock, ice, ore and crystal with the mining laser (the plasma cutter is faster), and smelt ore into bars at a furnace. Build floors, walls, doors and airlocks to seal rooms, then power them (solar, batteries) and keep the air on (oxygen generators and tanks). Farms, medbays, workbenches, drills and turrets come after. Crew: take in survivors and give them jobs. Nights bring the scrapper drones. Turrets help. So does a rifle. Inspired by Junon.io.

title: Story of Varandia
summary: Render Productions' tabletop game of Chaotic and Controlled magic: the Tome of rules, the character builder and sheets, spells, items, and campaigns with your group.
text: Story of Varandia is a tabletop world of Chaotic and Controlled magic, played with a d20. Raw, Chaotic magic gives the world its life. Train it into Controlled magic, carve it into runes, and carry it into the fight, so long as your Stamina holds. The rules are still being written. The Tome The rulebook, a chapter at a time: races , classes , stats and dice , magic and its eleven elements, the spellbook and the armory . The Bestiary lives in your GM's own book. Characters The builder walks you through it: roll your stats, pick a race and class, and fill in the sheet. Your sheet tracks Health and Stamina, your spells (cast straight from the sheet), your Satchel and Cardinal Items (anything in them can be enchanted with an element's rune), and lets you roll stats, saving throws and attacks from it. Your characters lists them all. Log in with Discord to keep them on any device. Campaigns A game master starts a campaign and shares its code; players join with their characters, and the GM sees everyone's sheet in one place. Add a Discord webhook and rolls post straight to your group's channel.

title: The Trading Floor
summary: Rend-Conomy as a Discord Activity: trade the market, play the Rend-Sino, check your farm and desk, and run any command, without leaving your voice channel.
text: The Trading Floor is RendConomy's Discord Activity: open it from the Activities button in a voice channel (or the app launcher) and the Rend-Conomy opens inside Discord. Your friends can see you're on the floor in your Discord status. What's on it The left side switches screens: the Market (pick a company to see its chart and trade it), the Rend-Sino , your Farm , your Desk and the Lake . The right side is a command line: type any command (without r! ) and the reply shows up with its buttons, the same as in chat. Games with buttons (blackjack, mines, the Rocket, heists, the Derby) work here too. It runs as you, in the server you opened it in. On phones, it needs the server's Activities turned on for mobile.

title: The Underground
summary: Mr. Glaz's black market: when and where he sets up, passwords, contraband, hot loot, laundering, smuggling, snitching, Heat and raids.
text: Every night from 10 PM to 4 AM Eastern , a figure in a red robe sets up somewhere on your server's city map. Mr. Glaz sells things Marquez won't, and buys things nobody should. Everything shady you do adds Heat , and Heat gets you raided. At a glance Open 10 PM–4 AM Eastern Command r!ug Heat 0–100, five stars Where he sets up He squats in a condemned building if there is one; otherwise in the most run-down place on the map (its owner loses half that day's rent); otherwise on an empty lot. He won't set up within a tile of a Police Station. If stations cover the whole map, he takes an alley off the map instead: there's always a password that night, and every deal there brings 50% more Heat. Password nights About one night in three, you need a password to get in. From 8 PM, Mr. Glaz hijacks one of TODD's drop-ins to leave it, hidden in a spoiler. Get in with r!ug <password> . Contraband Four of these are for sale each night ( r!ug buy <item> ): Hot loot Clean heists sometimes drop hot loot. Holding it adds Heat every day. Fence it ( r!ug fence ): half its value when it's fresh, rising to 90% after three days. Launder it through a Corner Shop you own ( r!ug launder ): its full value, a day later. Smuggling Once a night, put up between ⬡500 and ⬡10,000 ( r!ug smuggle <amount> ). Two hours later it comes back with 50% on top, 10% on top, or not at all (caught, with a lot of Heat). A Lighthouse lowers the chance of getting caught. Snitching For ⬡250 , tip TODD off about another player ( r!ug snitch @player ). If they're at three stars or more, they're raided and you get a reward plus a share of their fine. If not, the Heat lands on you. Heat and raids Heat runs from 0 to 100, shown as stars, and cools by 10 a day. The more stars, the more likely a raid: TODD confiscates your contraband and loot and fines you a tenth of your Polygons (up to ⬡5,000). At 100 Heat you're locked out for two nights. r!ug heat shows yours.

title: Work
summary: Jobs at the five house companies: shifts every 15 minutes, rush tasks, reviews and promotions, gigs and odd jobs.
text: Every house company on the market is also an employer. Get hired, work a shift every 15 minutes, answer the task it gives you, and climb from the bottom rank to the top. Your pay follows your company's share price, so a booming company pays better. Player companies are employers too: their pay follows their level, and their share price once they're public (see Player companies ). At a glance Shift every 15 min Gig every 10 min Base pay ⬡35 Ranks 4 per company The jobs Apply with r!apply <ticker> . Each company has its own kind of task and its own four ranks; the multiplier after each rank is how much more it pays than the first. Shifts and tasks r!work hands you a task: sort a mod queue, build a nacho order, put building steps in order, crunch numbers, spot a bug. Type the answer in the channel. You have about 20 seconds. Right and fast: full pay, plus a tip of up to 50% for speed. Wrong or too slow: you still get 40% . Rush: after a right answer there's a 20% chance another task comes in (up to 5 in a row). Rush tasks pay only if they're right. Coworkers: people working in the same channel within two minutes add 15% each (up to 3 ). Pay: ⬡35 × the company's price compared to where it started × your rank. Bastardly Glory's swings are capped so its pay stays sane. r!job shows your rank, accuracy, next review and next shift; r!job remind on pings you when a shift is ready. Reviews and promotions Every 10 shifts you get a review. Get 8 or more right and you're promoted; 4 or fewer and you're demoted. A great review at the top rank pays a bonus instead. You can quit 24 hours after being hired ( r!quit ), and you keep your rank if you come back. LAYOFFS If your company goes bankrupt, you're laid off with a few shifts' pay. A Hard Hat from Marquez keeps your job through one layoff. Gigs and odd jobs Gigs ( r!gig ): no job needed, every 10 minutes, pays 40% of a first-rank shift. Begging ( r!beg ): once an hour. ? of the time someone gives you ⬡ ? – ? , ? a cheap item from Marquez's shelf, otherwise nothing. Rich beggars get noticed: from a net worth of ? there's a ? chance you're caught ( ? from ? , ? from ? ). Then TODD fines you ? of your wallet (at most ? ), or Marquez just tells you off. Odd jobs ( r!oddjob ): a math problem, an unscramble, a count or a reverse. Answer in the channel within 90 seconds; up to 10 a day. Items that help Coffee resets your work cooldown. Overtime makes your next shift pay double. Hard Hat keeps your job through one layoff. Look out for the Labor Shortage and Hiring Spree world events , which raise pay for an hour.
